details.label: Discussion
details.text: A small cluster of storms has recently become somewhat better organized south and southwest of Jamestown, ND, with a recent gust of 77 mph observed in McIntosh County. The 00Z ABR sounding depicted substantial CINH for surface-based parcels, though considerably weaker CINH and strong buoyancy for parcels rooted around 850 mb. This thermodynamic profile within a modest warm-advection regime may allow for persistence of the ongoing cluster into late evening as it moves southeastward, assuming the cold pool remains sufficiently strong. Severe gusts (potentially near/above 75 mph) will remain possible with this cluster as it moves into northeast SD, while isolated hail will also be possible with the strongest embedded cells. WW 624 has been expanded in order to address this threat
